note: Narration for demo-video.html. Generated with edge-tts (Microsoft neural TTS); not an actor recording.

lines.n01: In Malaysia, some of our oldest stories are told in shadow.
lines.n02: Wayang Kulit is a traditional shadow puppet theatre, and a living intangible cultural heritage. Behind a lit screen, one master puppeteer, the Tok Dalang, moves every leather puppet, and gives every character a voice.
lines.n03: Today, fewer young people sit in front of that screen. So we asked: what happens when a heritage art meets storytelling technology?
lines.n04: We kept what makes shadow play special: the screen, the puppet, and the rods. Then we handed the rods to you. With camera-based AR, your own hand, tracked live, moves the puppet, and moves the story.
lines.n05: Because when you play a part, the story stays with you. Our story needed a hero who was left behind.
lines.n06: NASA's Opportunity rover landed on Mars in 2004. It was built for ninety days, and kept exploring for more than fourteen years, until a dust storm silenced it in 2018.
lines.n11: Everything runs in the browser. Hand tracking happens right on your device. Nothing is recorded, and every act also works with a mouse.
lines.n12: Shadows Left Behind. A Malaysian heritage art, retold with technology, so that what is left behind is never forgotten.
lines.n13: Now, let's see it in action.
